clearedSpotChecks.check: Rerun of battery.py (99,985 vectors) and targeted.py (85,544 vectors) on the seven chains on 2026-11-24: MULMOD and ADDMOD near 2^256-1, the 512 bit mulDiv product, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, BYTE, SHL, SHR, SAR, EXP, the comparisons, JUMPI conditions, KECCAK256, MCOPY and CALLDATALOAD at their edges.
clearedSpotChecks.note: battery.json and targeted.json show mismatchCount 0 and no errors for chains 10, 8453, 130, 7777777, 480, 57073 and 1868. I ran 32 vectors of my own as creation code eth_calls against the RPC URLs in networks.json on 2026-11-24. They cover MULMOD(2^256-1, 2^256-1, 2^256-2), MULMOD(a, b, not(0)) as in FullMath.sol:24, ADDMOD at 2^256-1, SDIV and SMOD of -2^255 by -1, SAR, SHL, SHR and BYTE with amounts 256, 2^32, 2^32+1, 2^64 and 2^64+3 (the truncation case of RUSTSEC-2026-0220), SIGNEXTEND(0, 0x80), EXP(2,255), EXP(3,161), DIV and MOD by zero, SLT and SGT at the sign bit, and KECCAK256 of 64 bytes. Every chain returned the specified word. Two first-run mismatches were errors in my expected values (ADDMOD(2^256-1, 1, 2^256-1) is 1, SGT(2^255, 0) is 0) and were identical on all seven chains. These opcodes are the ones FullMath.sol:24,48,112, BitMath.sol:16-45 and TickBitmap.sol:38,67,73 use. OSV lists for ruint only RUSTSEC-2025-0137 and RUSTSEC-2026-0220, and for revm-interpreter nothing, which agrees with cleared item 7.

clearedSpotChecks.note: rust/op-revm/src/evm.rs at op-reth/v2.9.0 imports EthInstructions (line 10), types OpEvm with EthInstructions<EthInterpreter, CTX> (lines 21 and 30) and builds it with EthInstructions::new_mainnet_with_spec (line 38). The web3_clientVersion strings I read were op-reth/v0.0.0-dev-unknown (OP Mainnet), reth/v2.5.2 base/v1.5.6 (Base), op-reth/v2.9.0-rc.1 (Unichain, Ink, Soneium), conduit-op-reth/v2.5.1 (Zora) and world-chain/v2.8.2 (World Chain), matching the clients the research file names.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Which block producing code could run a different EVM path than the public endpoint: external builders behind rollup-boost, and the fault proof programs.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The rollup-boost sidecar page states that rollup-boost validates the builder block with the proposer's execution client using engine_newPayload and returns the local fallback block if the external block is invalid. A builder that computes an opcode differently therefore yields a rejected block, not a different PoolManager state. Acting on a builder or proof fault needs the sequencer, builder or proposer, so actor operator is right.
